The user has labeled the windows of the design file "F2/design_confidence_300_s0.json", and the filled sheet is "F2/labels_confidence_300_s0.csv". They are asking for the error rate of this map. This corresponds to "olmoearth_estimate_map_error", which uses the "design_path" and "labels_path" parameters.

According to the tool description: "How wrong is my map / how should N labels be spent... The interval is obtained from olmoearth_estimate_map_error. The inferencex additional package is required." Also, "Report the returned estimate, low, high, and method as-is. Do not substitute p ± 1.96√(p(1-p)/n)."

So I need to call "olmoearth_estimate_map_error" with "design_path = F2/design_confidence_300_s0.json" and "labels_path = F2/labels_confidence_300_s0.csv".

Let's execute that call.

per_class.method: stratified by confidence margin: ratios of Horvitz-Thompson totals with linearised variance; shares as Horvitz-Thompson totals

interval_rules: A targeted review set (e.g. the windows olmoearth_review_set lists) is not a sample: its error rate overstates the map's, 1.8 to 5.8 times on the package's exp78.

The simple-random-sample interval p +/- 1.96 sqrt(p(1 - p)/n) does not apply to a stratified or targeted design, nor to a pool of both; report the interval and method olmoearth_estimate_map_error returns instead.
result.report: Report the estimate with [low, high] and the method string as returned; the rate is of the design's population windows.
next_steps: Report the estimate with its interval and method as returned (the fact whole_map_estimate states them); the rate is of the design's population.
Name the weakest classes as the fact weakest_classes ranks them (by user's accuracy, over classes with at least 5 map-labelled windows), not from the table by eye.

No zone can be certified from this confidence design: olmoearth_certify_zone needs design='random'. A certified zone needs a new plan with design='random', every drawn window labelled, and alpha, delta and rule fixed before labelling. A random design makes a certified zone possible, not certain: olmoearth_certify_zone may certify nothing.
A narrower interval needs more labels under a new plan with a larger budget, fixed before any of its labels is seen.

facts.sentence: The map's error rate is estimated at 19.4% (95% interval 15.7% to 23.6%) from 300 labelled windows of a population of 15813; method: stratified by confidence margin; Wilson interval on the design's effective sample size.

Ranked by user's accuracy (of the windows the map puts in a class, the share the labels agree with) over the 5 classes with at least 5 map-labelled windows, the lowest are class 5 (0 of 10 correct; 0.0%, 95% interval 0.0% to 27.8%), class 1 (2 of 9 correct; 22.5%, 95% interval 6.5% to 55.0%) and class 6 (20 of 44 correct; 45.1%, 95% interval 32.3% to 58.6%). Classes 0, 2 and 8 have fewer than 5 map-labelled windows (0, 2 and 1), too few to rank. Under this design each estimate is weighted, so it need not equal correct over labelled.

forbidden_claims.why: this design is stratified, so a simple-random-sample interval (p +/- 1.96 sqrt(p(1 - p)/n)) does not apply to it, nor any interval worked out by hand; the interval is [low, high] by the method returned (stratified by confidence margin; Wilson interval on the design's effective sample size)

this design is 'confidence', not 'random': a certified zone's guarantee needs the labels inside each candidate zone to be a random sample of it, which a stratified draw is not, so no zone can be certified from these labels (olmoearth_certify_zone refuses them); certification needs a new plan with design='random', which makes a certified zone possible, not certain

a random design makes a certified zone possible, never certain: olmoearth_certify_zone certifies a zone only where the labels drawn in it hold few enough errors for its exact test, so it may certify none, and no design, sample size, budget or plan can promise a certified (or 'certifiable') region, or a zone of any size; these labels of a confidence design cannot certify at all, and a new random plan may certify nothing

text: The result is clear. I'll report the estimate with the interval and method attached, along with the weakest class.

content:
**Map error rate: 19.4%** (95% interval **15.7% – 23.6%**) from 300 labelled windows of a population of 15,813. Method: stratified by confidence margin; Wilson interval on the design's effective sample size (effective n ≈ 384). Overall accuracy: ~80.6%.

Weakest classes by user's accuracy (classes with ≥5 map-labelled windows):

| Class | Correct / labelled | User accuracy (95%) |
|---|---|---|
| 5 | 0 / 10 | 0.0% [0.0%, 27.8%] |
| 1 | 2 / 9 | 22.5% [6.5%, 55.0%] |
| 6 | 20 / 44 | 45.1% [32.3%, 58.6%] |

Notes:
- Classes 0, 2, 8 had too few labelled windows to rank reliably.
- A certified zone can't be drawn from this confidence design — that requires a new plan with `design='random'`. Say the word if you want one set up.
